## Background

- Food and agriculture researchers face growing obstacles to using data:
  - Limited and/or time-consuming discoverability of datasets  
  - Barriers to access (e.g. cost, application processes, restricted use)  
  - Lack of standards for citation, metadata, and linkage

## Background

- Meanwhile, demand for interoperable data-driven research is rising:
  - Policymakers and funders want more *evidence-based* insights  
  - Reviewers and editors are being asked to review submissions with more complex data  
  - Early-career researchers struggle to know where or how to start


## The Initiative

This project responds by building tools that:

(1) surface food + ag data (search and discovery)
(2) connect researchers (citability)
(3) contextualize food + ag data (metadata standardization)


## Why This Work Matters (Big Picture)

- Federal data systems are under strain
- Financial resources are bleak
- Many food + ag datasets are fragmented, underused, or difficult to access
- Researchers in food + ag are missing opportunities to contribute 


## Does This Infrastructure Already Exist?

In short, no.<br>

The components are there, but none are tailored specifically for food + ag.

## What We’re Building

- Metadata & research navigation layers  
- Linked dashboards (e.g., [USDA FAR Dashboard](https://democratizingdata.ai/tools/dashboard/food-agricultural-research/), [Digital Science Data Explorer](https://appserver.democratizingdata.ai/), [National Data Platform](https://nationaldataplatform.org/))
- Researcher-facing tools to:
  - Discover data sources
  - Find collaborators (and referees!)
  - See who funds what
  - More...

## Why AJAE?

- High volume of applied research with policy relevance  
- Referees increasingly being asked to review submissions using linked or nontraditional datasets  
- Gaps in data transparency can slow publication process or cause confusion  
- Editors have no shared tools to support “data-aware” peer review  

**We’re seeing:**

- Sourcing for food + ag datasets in replication appendices not always available
- New datasets being used for research published in high-quality journals - how do we validate these?
- Growing need for guidance around restricted-use and proprietary data citation


## What Data Are Researchers Actually Using?

We reviewed thousands of food security publications to identify dataset usage.

**Finding:**

> 11 commonly used food and agriculture datasets account for **only 2%** of all research published on food security.

<small>Read more [here](https://laurenchenarides.github.io/data_usage_report/report.html) and [here](presentation-cfare.qmd).</small>

**So what *is* being used?**
We’re cataloging and analyzing those patterns to inform future infrastructure needs.

- Most food security research is **not** using USDA, ERS, or Census-linked datasets
- Many are drawing on novel, proprietary, or administrative sources
- Citation patterns suggest major discoverability and standardization gaps



## Supporting Editors & Reviewers

We’re building tools and infrastructure to help editors and reviewers navigate a data-rich publication landscape.  

We’re looking for feedback to help make these resources useful in real editorial contexts.

Current project outputs of interest:

- Draft technical paper for publication  
- Early access to tools

:::{.callout-note icon=false title="Our Vision"}

To build a trusted, transparent, and researcher-informed data infrastructure that supports food and agricultural research.

- Centered on usability, not just access  
- Built with — not just for — the research community  
- Designed to help different user communities (researchers, reviewers, and policymakers) make better decisions  

A future where food and ag researchers can:

- Find the right data — quickly  
- Understand how it’s been used  
- Trust the infrastructure behind it  
- Build on each other’s work — not start from scratch — and get attribution
